Package de.nexus.antixray.api.event

Klasse BypassChangeEvent

java.lang.Object
org.bukkit.event.Event
org.bukkit.event.player.PlayerEvent
de.nexus.antixray.api.event.BypassChangeEvent
public class BypassChangeEvent extends org.bukkit.event.player.PlayerEvent
Called after the effective bypass of a player has changed, that is whenever NexusAntiXRayApi.isBypassed(org.bukkit.entity.Player) starts to return a different value for the player.

The event reports changes only. Setting the session switch to the state the player already has, or a permission change that is covered by the session switch, calls nothing. Every player starts a session without bypass: a player who joins with the permission nexusantixray-autobypass gets one event with cause BypassChangeEvent.Cause.PERMISSION during the join. No event is called when a player leaves.

The event is a notification and cannot be cancelled. When it is called the change is already in effect and the player's chunks are being sent again. To overrule a change, call NexusAntiXRayApi.setBypass(org.bukkit.entity.Player, boolean) from the handler.

Order

The events of one player are called one after the other, in the order in which the changes happened, and never nested. If a handler changes the bypass itself, that change takes effect at once, but its event is called only after the current event has been delivered to all listeners. A listener that follows isBypassed() from event to event therefore always ends up with the real state, whatever its priority.

wasBypassed() and isBypassed() describe the change this event is about. A later change may already be in effect while the handler runs (its event is still to come); ask NexusAntiXRayApi.isBypassed(org.bukkit.entity.Player) for the state right now.

Two plugins that overrule each other from their handlers would go on forever. NexusAntiXRay stops calling the event for a player after a few dozen changes in a row, logs a warning that names the listening plugins and drops the remaining calls of that run. The state itself stays whatever was set last.

Thread

The event is synchronous. It is always called on the thread that ticks the player: the server thread, on Folia the region thread that owns the player. It is never called from a network or ray tracing thread.

A change can be made from any thread (/nax bypass <player> from the console, NexusAntiXRayApi.setBypass(org.bukkit.entity.Player, boolean) from an asynchronous task). The event is then handed over to the player's thread and called there a moment later. Do not rely on the event having been called when the call that made the change returns: that is not the case for a change from another thread or from inside a handler of this event. If the player leaves before the hand-over, the event is dropped.

1.0.0
